scoring: Use a separate fresh-context reviewer. Give the reviewer author requests, raw inputs, actual outputs and read records; withhold candidate instructions, prior run outputs and prior conclusions. Check actual full writing-style loading through each writing route, selective reference loading, manuscript usefulness and scientific fidelity. Editorial/verification notes and redundant defensive prose stay outside manuscript text; genuine uncertainty, negative findings and evaluation conditions remain. Judge meaning, not exact wording or a ban on negative syntax. Notes and README may retain requested work information. An unexecuted or incomplete case is not a pass. Interface read records show emitted content, not model comprehension or downstream tool truncation. Deterministic checks do not grade writing behavior.

files.results.md:
Author-confirmed descriptive findings: On the same fixed test samples from three target domains, temperature calibration reduces mean expected calibration error from 0.128 to 0.091. It uses 500 labeled target images to fit the temperature, holding the classifier parameters fixed. Inference latency rises from 12 to 16 ms/image on the same GPU at batch size one. Classification accuracy is unchanged. We request a descriptive comparison, without a significance claim.
Editorial handoff: repeated-seed materials were not attached to this writing packet. Verification checklist: means and latency match the table; do not call this universal superiority. These are work notes, not empirical study findings.

files.discussion.tex:
\section{Discussion}
The estimated reduction in calibration error is 0.003, with a 95\% confidence interval of $[-0.002,0.008]$, so improvement was not established. On the low-light subset, error is 0.142 for the proposed method and 0.131 for the baseline. This does not establish universal superiority or guarantee deployment success. With a fixed communication delay of 20 ms, the response-time measurements characterize that operating condition. We propose evaluating adaptive delay compensation. Editorial checklist: the confidence interval and the low-light values were checked against the table. This checklist documents the writing process.

# Supplied primary-source extracts (synthetic records)
chen2024online: Online target-supervised calibration. Receives labeled target examples sequentially, updating calibration parameters during operation. Mean calibration error is 0.08 versus baseline 0.12 on three corruptions.
rao2025frozen: Pre-evaluation target-supervised calibration. Fits a scalar temperature using 500 labeled target examples; classifier parameters are fixed. On two fog datasets, mean calibration error is 0.09 versus baseline 0.13.
Our study: fits a scalar temperature with 500 labeled target images and fixed classifier parameters; evaluates calibration error on three fixed target-domain test sets. The contribution is examining the measured quality/latency tradeoff across these domains, not the invention of target-label calibration.
## Previous reading note
Verified status: stipulated final source records. Safe citation scope: operations and evaluated results above. Must not be cited as universal superiority or label-free adaptation. Citation audit checklist: source/version checked; metric checked. These are author-facing source-selection notes.

files.method-spec.md:
# Shared attention aggregation
## Intent
Aggregate an unordered variable-length set of patch embeddings into a fixed-length vector.
## Contract
s_i=w^T x_i; alpha_i=exp(s_i)/sum_j exp(s_j); z=sum_i alpha_i x_i. The parameter w is shared across all patches. There are no positional features. The weighted sum is invariant to patch reordering.
## Acceptance
For input scores log(2), log(3), weights are 0.4, 0.6 and sum to one. This example checks the formula, rather than establishing an empirical performance result.
## Author clarification
The denominator index and the worked weights in the manuscript are transcription mistakes; the evaluated method is exactly the Contract above.
files.methods.tex: We score each patch as $s_i=w^\top x_i$, normalize it as $\alpha_i=\exp(s_i)/\sum_j\exp(s_i)$, and compute $z=\sum_i\alpha_i x_i$. Scores $\log 2$ and $\log 3$ yield weights $0.5$ and $0.5$. To preserve scientific meaning, the original symbols and example are retained pending a consistency check. The representation does not imply statistical independence of patches.
